A declaration of yellow alert status over the Visayas grid is expected on Sunday, November 22 due to tight energy reserves, the National Grid Corporation of the Philippines (NGCP) said.
In an advisory, the yellow alert status will take place between 5 p.m. to 9 p.m.
The grid is currently running on an available capacity of 2,380 megawatts (MW) although the peak demand is 2,347 MW.
The yellow alert status declaration is due to the unavailability of several coal plants in the Visayas region.
There will be unplanned outages of Therma Visayas Inc. 2 and Palinpinon I Geothermal Power Plant Unit 1.
Meanwhile, there are planned outages on Palm Concepcion Power Corporation and KEPCO SPC Power Corporation Unit 2.
Further, the NGCP said that there is a limited transfer capacity of Mindanao-Visayas interconnection due to scheduled maintenance of Baloi-Kauswagan 230kV Line 1.
Meanwhile, eight plants are on forced outage in November, one plant since October, two plants since September, two plants since August, one plant since June, three plants since 2025, one plant since 2024, two plants since 2023, and one plant since 2021. There are also 21 plants running on derated capacities, for a total of 668.4MW unavailable to the grid.
A yellow alert is issued when the operating margin is insufficient to meet the transmission grid’s contingency requirement.
To address the thinning energy reserves in the Visayas grid, the Department of Energy (DOE) earlier ordered the NGCP to install over 250 megawatts of battery energy storage system.
The Energy Regulatory Commission (ERC) also earlier issued 24 show-cause orders (SCO) against 13 power generation companies over power outages that hit the Visayas and Mindanao. —Vince Angelo Ferreras/RF, GMA News

Yellow alert issued for 21 provinces! Heavy rainfall in the east, southwesterly storm in Istanbul tomorrow
22.11.2026 10:03
The General Directorate of Meteorology (MGM) issued a yellow-code warning for 21 provinces, including Rize, Trabzon, Erzurum, Diyarbakır, and Hatay. Heavy rainfall is expected in the Eastern Black Sea, Eastern and Southeastern Anatolia, and the Eastern Mediterranean, while winds reaching 60 kilometers per hour are expected on the Western Black Sea coast. AKOM reported that no precipitation is expected in Istanbul today, while a southerly storm (lodos) will be effective tomorrow.
Rainy weather continues to be effective in the eastern parts of the country. According to the Meteorology's forecasts for today, partly and very cloudy weather will prevail across the country. Precipitation is expected to be locally heavy in some provinces.
YELLOW-CODE WARNING FOR 21 PROVINCES
The provinces for which a yellow-code warning was issued for Sunday, November 22 in MGM's MeteoWarning system are as follows:
Ardahan, Artvin, Batman, Bayburt, Bingöl, Diyarbakır, Erzincan, Erzurum, Giresun, Gümüşhane, Hatay, Kahramanmaraş, Muş, Ordu, Osmaniye, Rize, Samsun, Sivas, Tokat, Trabzon and Tunceli.
According to the daily forecast report, rain is expected in 18 provinces. A thunderstorm warning was issued for Hatay, Kahramanmaraş and Osmaniye.
REGIONS WHERE HEAVY RAIN IS EXPECTED
Precipitation is expected to be locally heavy in Rize and Artvin surroundings and the eastern districts of Trabzon. In Eastern Anatolia, heavy rain is expected in the southeast of the region and around Bingöl, Ağrı and Iğdır. It was reported that precipitation in Van will intensify after the night hours.
In Southeastern Anatolia, the surroundings of Diyarbakır, Batman and Siirt are within the scope of a local heavy rain warning. Intermittent showers and thunderstorms are also forecast in the east of the Eastern Mediterranean.
SNOW WILL FALL IN HIGHER AREAS
In the Eastern Black Sea and Eastern Anatolia, precipitation is expected to be in the form of sleet and, in places, snow in high areas above 2,000 meters. Intermittent rain and showers are also expected around Kayseri and Sivas.
WIND WILL REACH 60 KILOMETERS PER HOUR
The wind blowing from southerly directions is expected to strengthen in the southeast of Eastern Anatolia and on the Western Black Sea coasts. It was reported that the wind speed in these regions may reach 40-60 kilometers per hour. In Marmara, Central Anatolia and the inland parts of the Western Black Sea, fog and mist may be seen in places during the morning hours.
AKOM: LODOS STORM IN ISTANBUL TOMORROW
The Istanbul Metropolitan Municipality Department of Disaster Affairs and Risk Management (AKOM) published its weekly weather forecast report dated November 21. According to the report, partly and slightly cloudy weather is expected in Istanbul today, with no precipitation forecast. The temperature is expected to range between 13 and 16 degrees.
AKOM reported that a lodos storm will be effective in the city on Monday, November 23, and precipitation will be seen in the evening hours. On Tuesday, November 24, temperatures are expected to drop sharply to 7 to 12 degrees.
WEATHER IN MAJOR CITIES
According to Meteorology data, today 16 degrees are expected in Istanbul, 11 in Ankara, 21 in İzmir, 25 in Antalya, and 24 in Adana. In the Eastern Black Sea, the temperature will be 16 degrees in Trabzon and Rize. The temperature is forecast to be 7 degrees in Erzurum, 15 in Diyarbakır, and 14 in Van.
